HEADLINE: Sector Briefing: Energy

BODY:
The S&P 500 (-0.3%) is off to a lower start with nine sectors holding early losses and energy (-2.4%) sitting at the bottom of the early leaderboard.

Key factors driving today's performance include:

Pressure from a lower price of oil as WTI crude slides past its 2025 low, falling $1.76, or 3.10%, to $55.06/bbl. This puts oil on track for its lowest pit close since early 2021 amid growing hopes for a Russia-Ukraine peace deal that will be acceptable to both sides, which would likely set the path for Russia's return to the global oil market. Downside leadership from names like Halliburton (HAL 27.11, -1.30, -4.58%), Phillips 66 (PSX 136.30, -5.21, -3.68%), and ConocoPhillips (COP 91.08, -3.28, -3.48%) deepen their recent reversals from multi-week highs.

Notable movers:

APA (APA 24.01, -1.26, -5.01%): weakest performer in the sector, falling back below its 50-day moving average (24.13). Diamondback Energy (FANG 146.84, -7.22, -4.69%): falling to its 50-day moving average (24.13). Halliburton (HAL 27.11, -1.30, -4.58%): deepening last week's reversal from its best level since January. Phillips 66 (PSX 136.30, -5.21, -3.68%): falling back to its 50-day moving average (135.84), continuing last week's reversal from its best level since August 2024. Baker Hughes (BKR 45.21, -1.68, -3.58%): falling to its lowest level since late October after finding resistance at its 50-day moving average (47.76). Company and Hunt Oil Company announced a joint framework for redevelopment of mature oil and gas fields. ConocoPhillips (COP 91.08, -3.28, -3.48%): falling past its 200-day moving average (92.26) toward its 50-day moving average (89.64). Johnson Rice downgraded the stock to Hold from Accumulate with a $105 target. Marathon Petroleum (MPC 179.15, -6.36, -3.43%): on track for its lowest close since late August. EQT Corp (EQT 53.29, -1.88, -3.41%): falling back below its 200-day moving average (54.03). Occidental Petroleum (OXY 38.86, -1.33, -3.31%): falling to its lowest level since early May. Valero (VLO 163.36, -4.54, -2.70%): falling to its lowest level in nearly two months. Exxon Mobil (XOM 115.18, -2.58, -2.20%): falling back below its 50-day moving average (115.69). Chevron (CVX 147.09, -2.71, -1.81%): on track for its lowest close since early July.  Kinder Morgan (KMI 26.43, -0.29, -1.10%): best performer in the sector, on track for its lowest close in nearly six weeks.
text: Energy stocks led broad market declines today as WTI crude fell 3.10% to $55.06/bbl, its lowest since early 2021, pressured by hopes for a Russia-Ukraine peace deal that could return Russian oil to global markets. Exxon Mobil (XOM) dropped 2.20% to $115.18, slipping below its 50-day moving average ($115.69), though it outperformed sector peers like APA, Diamondback, and Halliburton, which fell 3.4%-5%. Chevron also underperformed, down 1.81%. While XOM's decline was less severe than many peers, the broader sector weakness—driven by falling oil prices and technical breakdowns—suggests continued pressure on energy equities if crude prices remain depressed.
